newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Coca-Cola and Venezuela partner fined.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola and Venezuela partner fined.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co and its Venezuelan partner were fined the equivalent of $1.9 million for forming a joint venture that violated the country's anti-trust regulations.

Venezuela's anti-monopoly commission (Procompetencia) ruled Tuesday that a deal signed in August between Coca-Cola and its partner Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela restricted free competition. The commission stopped short of blocking the venture, however.

Coca-Cola's deal with Venezuela's largest bottler ended Grupo Cisneros's 50-year-old collaboration with PepsiCo. Afterwards, Pepsi products virtually disappeared from the Venezuelan market, where the company once commanded an 80 percent share.

A Coca-Cola spokeswoman in Caracas said the company would probably appeal Procompetencia's the fine, saying the amount was "unreasonable." Company lawyers are reviewing the ruling in detail, the spokewoman, Maria Teresa Almarza, said.
Still, the ruling "ratified that the venture was legal and valid" and Coke was therefore "very pleased," she said.
PepsiCo had filed suit in August charging that the venture created a monopoly, preventing freedom of choice in the Venezuelan soft-drinks market.
Procompetencia, however, did not accept Pepsi's request to declare the venture illegal, the release said.

Among the changes ordered by Procompetencia, Coke must come up with a different plan for selling its 18 Venezuelan bottling plants. Coke and Cisneros are also prohibited from offering two brands of any single flavor of soft drink.
Alberto Uribe, head of Pepsi's Andean region, said the ruling "restored free competition in the market and severely punished Coca-Cola."

He acknowledged in a statement that the commission's ruling "will not give (Pepsi) full access to the market in the short term even if it will dismantle barriers that Coca-Cola sought to erect through its monopolistic venture."
